sections.h2: How is property tax set up for a house seller in Alamance County?
sections.html:
A single county department handles listing, valuation and collection of taxes on everything taxable. The department is at 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and its phone line is (336) 228-1312.

The county was formed in 1849 from part of Orange County and covers about 434 square miles. Graham is the seat and Burlington is the largest community. The towns of Elon, Haw River, Green Level, Ossipee, Swepsonville and Alamance, plus parts of Mebane and Gibsonville, fall inside the county. Textile mills along the Haw River drove its early growth.

Four things shape a sale here: the January 1 listing date, the September 1 due date, the 2027 revaluation, and a delinquent tax check at recording. Each gets its own section below.

sections.h2: What is the Alamance County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
Land Records explains that each parcel is listed to whoever owned it on January 1, and that date fixes the tax year. Statements go out in July, and the county charges no interest on a payment made by January 5.

Alamance County tax calendar and relief deadlines
DateWhat happens
January 1Listing date; owner on this day is billed
January 1 to 31Filing window for present-use and exemption applications
June 1Deadline for elderly, disabled, circuit breaker and disabled veteran relief
JulyBills mailed
September 1Bills due
January 5Last day to pay with no interest
January 6Delinquent; 2% interest added, then 0.75% on the sixth of each later month

A purchase that closes after January 1 can still produce a bill in the previous owner's name, even though the deed is recorded and the county has updated its record. Getting the mailing address corrected before July is the surest way to receive the bill on time.

Payment options are by mail (counted by postmark), in an indoor or outdoor drop box (credited as of the drop date), or online with a convenience fee. Registered vehicles are billed separately by the state through Tag and Tax Together at registration renewal.

sections.h2: What is happening with the 2027 revaluation in Alamance County?
sections.html:
Alamance County is revaluing every parcel effective January 1, 2027, and notices of value are scheduled to be mailed February 15, 2027. The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2023. North Carolina requires reappraisal at least every eight years under G.S. 105-286, and the county has chosen a four-year cycle.

Vincent Valuations, which assisted with the 2023 work, is performing the 2027 appraisal. Staff spend roughly two years in the field checking property features, comparing sales, and noting improvements. The county says its goal is to reach, or come close to, 100% of market value at revaluation.

A bigger number on the notice need not produce a bigger bill. County staff say rates fall as values rise, and a revenue neutral rate would keep the typical owner near last year's payment. Parcels that gained more than the average pay more, while laggards pay less.

If you plan to sell in 2027, open the notice the day it arrives. Your appeal period runs from its date, and late filings are generally turned away. The revaluation hotline is the same number as the tax department, (336) 228-1312.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a property value in Alamance County?
sections.html:
County appraisers hear informal reviews first. If that does not settle things, the matter moves to the Board of Equalization and Review. Filing windows differ by property type.

  • Real property: during the annual listing period, with documentation such as sales, photos, repair estimates or an appraisal.
  • Business and individual personal property: thirty days from the notice of value.
  • Registered vehicles: thirty days after the due date shown on the combined tag and tax notice.

The state outlines what comes next. The local board starts deliberating about the first week of April and allots each side a fixed time. A losing owner can go to the Property Tax Commission in Raleigh, a trial-style body that follows evidence rules and puts the burden on the taxpayer.

The county lists three typical grounds: a value above likely sale price, wrong square footage or condition on the record, and nearby sales pointing lower. It supplies a comparable sales tool and a property record search to help you gather proof.

sections.h2: What tax relief programs can Alamance County homeowners use?
sections.html:
June 1 is the usual filing deadline, and income caps change yearly, so get current figures from the tax department. An online eligibility calculator on the county site covers four of the programs.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: a seniors-and-disabled benefit that shelters the larger of $25,000 or half the home's taxable value, subject to an income cap.
  • Circuit breaker deferral: postpones part of the tax on a permanent residence, scaled to income. Eligible owners are 65 or older, or disabled, with five years of ownership and residence behind them.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: shelters the first $45,000 of assessed value for an honorably discharged veteran with a total, permanent service-connected disability, or for a surviving spouse. Age and income do not matter.
  • Present-use value: taxes qualifying farm, horticulture and forestry land on its use, but taxes deferred for the previous three years can be recaptured if the land leaves the program.

An owner who sells while a deferral or present-use status is in place should ask about payoff or recapture amounts before agreeing to a closing date.

sections.h2: What does Alamance County check about taxes when a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds states that every deed recorded after May 2, 2011, except timber deeds and releases, must go before the county Tax Department for delinquent tax certification first. That step follows G.S. 161-31(b). A seller with back taxes should plan to clear them so the certification can be issued.

After recording, the change reaches the property record through a short chain. The Register of Deeds keeps the document and gives it a book and page number. Land Records staff review it, change the owner name and mailing address, and push the update to the online record and GIS map. A simple sale of an existing parcel moves faster than a split or a new subdivision. If you do not see the change after several weeks, call Land Records with the book and page number.

If an owner has died, the county follows the estate file at the Clerk of Superior Court or recorded documents. Bills stay due on schedule meanwhile, and staff ask for the estate file number, the parcel number or address, and a mailing address.

sections.h2: Which housing figures stand out in Alamance County?
sections.html:
The 2020 count was 171,415 residents, and the July 2025 estimate of 186,177 is 8.6% above the 2020 base. Houses carry a $241,500 median value for 2020 to 2024, owners live in 65.0% of homes, and the county has 70,062 households. Median gross rent was $1,064 and median household income was $65,651.

Builders took out 2,027 permits in 2025. Poverty stood at 13.8%, and workers averaged 25.9 minutes of travel to work.

Look up your own parcel in the county property record search before you pick an asking price.

faqs.q: When are Alamance County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due September 1. Interest does not start until January 6, so a bill paid by January 5 carries none. After that, 2% is added, plus 0.75% on the sixth of each following month.

faqs.q: Whose name is on the bill after an early-year purchase?
faqs.a: A bill can still arrive under the prior owner's name, because the county lists parcels to the January 1 owner. Divide the cost at closing and fix the mailing address before July.

faqs.q: When will new values from the 2027 revaluation arrive?
faqs.a: Notices of value are scheduled to be mailed February 15, 2027, for the January 1, 2027 effective date. Your appeal deadline is tied to the date on that notice.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for tax relief programs in Alamance County?
faqs.a: June 1 for the elderly or disabled exclusion, the circuit breaker deferral and the disabled veteran exclusion. Present-use and exemption filings fall in the January listing window.

faqs.q: Who do I call at Alamance County Tax Administration?
faqs.a: Call (336) 228-1312 or visit 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The same number handles revaluation questions.
